FAQs

What is a Welding Electrode?

When connected to a welding machine, a welding electrode imbued with diverse metals or filler melds under intense electrical heat, fusing disparate metal parts with a resilient, polished bond.

How do you use the correct welding electrode?

Consider the base metal, desired properties, thickness, position, and service conditions to tailor the welding process effectively.

What is a welding wire?  

A slender metallic rod welding wire ignites to produce a heated arc, softening under applied heat to fuse metal pieces together.

What is the purpose of MIG Welding?

Metal Inert Gas (MIG) welding employs an arc welding technique in which a continuous solid wire is heated and fed into the weld pool through a welding torch.

What is the purpose of TIG Welding?

Tungsten Inert Gas (TIG) welding, or Gas Tungsten Arc welding (GTAW), involves joining metals by heating them with an arc created between a tungsten electrode and the parent metals.
